Background technology

The such as isolator of the isolator of photo-coupler, inducer coupling, capacitor coupling and the isolation element of GMR (giant magnetoresistance) element separation device are currently used as the device for sending signal between multiple semiconductor chips, and each semiconductor chip works on different supply voltages.

Such as, photo-coupler uses a chip to convert electrical signals to optical signal, then uses another chip that optical signal is converted to the signal of telecommunication, therefore provides isolation between two semiconductor chips. The isolator of inducer coupling uses a coil to convert electrical signals to magnetic, then uses another coil that this magnetic is converted to the signal of telecommunication, thereby ensure that the isolation between two semiconductor chips. The isolator of capacitor coupling uses an electrode of capacity cell to convert electrical signals to electric field, then uses another electrode of this element that electric field is converted to the signal of telecommunication, thus provides isolation between two semiconductor chips. GMR element isolator uses coil to convert electrical signals to magnetic, then uses GMR element that this magnetic is converted to the signal of telecommunication, thus provides isolation between two semiconductor chips.

Above-mentioned isolation element is used in the power control circuit of today of such as inverter device and Changer Device. Specifically, the such power control circuit in the last few years worked in a power-supply system sends the control signal from microcomputer output via isolation element to the chip of another power-supply system, and thus the voltage level of changeover control signal is in question. Power control circuit carries out using gate drivers to amplify the control signal that its voltage level is converted, then the control signal of amplification is fed to the control terminal of power transistor (output transistor), and this control terminal control flows through the electric current of load.
